title: MA Protocol: Intratympanic Injection
desc: MA workflow for SSNHL order creation, day-of intratympanic injection setup, EMR documentation, and follow-up scheduling.

blocks.content: When SSNHL is suspected — same day or initial visit
When a patient presents with sudden hearing loss, the physician will prescribe a high-dose prednisone taper. At that visit, create an order in the EMR.
Impression: "Sudden hearing loss"
Plan: "Order in-office procedure"
Under procedure details: select intratympanic membrane injection
Task the order to the in-office procedure insurance coordinator for verification

Intratympanic injection is only performed after the patient completes the prednisone course and returns for a repeat audiogram approximately one week later. Whether injection proceeds depends on the patient's audiogram response to prednisone.
Day of injection — before the procedure
Confirm the procedure has been insurance-verified by the coordinator — check the order and its notes before doing anything else. Do not proceed if verification is not confirmed.
Obtain signed consent form — located in the PDF manager in the EMR, searchable as "chemical labyrinthotomy"
Draw dexamethasone 10 mg/mL, 0.4 mL into a 1 mL syringe using a 22-gauge needle, then switch to a 27-gauge needle for the physician to inject with
Place 1–2 drops of phenol into a small cup using the phenol dropper
Grab the phenol applicator
Place the vial, loaded syringe, cup with phenol, and phenol applicator together in a basin and hand it to the physician
EMR documentation at time of procedure
Use diagnosis "Sudden hearing loss" with plan "chemical labyrinthotomy"
Under procedure details, make sure to include the medication used — enter "dexamethasone" explicitly. If the medication is not entered, it will not be charged with the procedure.
After the injection
Patient must lie flat with the injected ear facing the ceiling for 30 minutes — this keeps the steroid in the middle ear space for absorption. Set a timer.
After 30 minutes, fit the patient with Doc's Proplugs earplug
Confirm with patient: any side effects, dizziness? Intermittent ear muffling is expected from the medication — reassure the patient this is normal
Emphasize wearing the Doc's plug in the shower for the next several weeks until the eardrum perforation is fully healed
Scheduling and follow-up
Patient is required to complete a brain MRI with IAC protocol
Schedule a follow-up in 1 week with audiology first, then the physician — for possible repeat intratympanic injection if hearing has not returned
Recommend the patient book weekly appointments for 3 weeks to ensure they are in the schedule, each with audiology first followed by the physician visit
